Hand-carved from a single, solid block of dense, rich African hardwood by the Lozi people of the Western Province (historically Barotseland) along the Zambezi River valley in Zambia, this mid-to-large-sized vessel features a beautifully streamlined silhouette topped with a stylized swimming duck finial that serves as a functional handle. Historically used to serve prepared meats and vegetables while keeping them warm, these bowls are highly prized today by collectors of global folk art, ethnographic artifacts, and organic mid-century modern design. The piece displays incredible, traditional craftsmanship. The thin, stepped inner lip of the lid is meticulously carved to form a flush, interlocking seal with the base. Inside, the continuous, rhythmic adze gouge marks remain clearly visible across the interior walls, proving it was hollowed entirely by hand rather than turned on a mechanical lathe. Boyd Crystal Art Glass was opened in October 1978 in Cambridge, OH. by father Bernard C.(former employee of Cambridge Glass Co. and Degenhart Glass Co,) and son Bernard F.
